newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine firms await wheat, corn price falls.
newsitem.headline: Philippine firms await wheat, corn price falls.

text.p: Philippine firms are expected to be on the lookout for bargains for wheat and corn next week, Manila grains traders said on Friday.
Traders said Philippine grains buyers were mostly out of the market this week on hopes prices would drop some more in the coming days.

Market talk on Friday was that Philippine flour millers Morning Star and Delta Milling had bought a combined shipment of 20,000 tonnes U.S. dark northern spring wheat and western white wheat through trading firm Cargill.
A spokesman of Cargill declined to confirm or deny the rumours while officers of the two firms could not be reached for comment.
Traders said Philippine firms had expressed an interest in buying up to 100,000 tonnes corn and 75,000 tonnes wheat for July and August arrivals.
"I'm waiting for U.S. wheat prices to drop before jumping on to the bandwagon," an executive at a local mill told Reuters.
Philippine traders said wheat prices rallied on Thursday after Pakistan bought 500,000 tonnes wheat, including 350,000 tonnes U.S. wheat.
The executive said his group planned to import 40,000 tonnes wheat for late July to August arrival.
Philippine feed mills, which also planned to import up to 100,000 tonnes of corn, said they were waiting for prices to drop.
